name: Safety Instrumented System Security
description: Covers the security of safety instrumented systems (SIS): SIS architecture and separation from the basic process control system, the interplay of IEC 61511 and IEC 61508 functional safety with IEC 62443 security, safety-security co-engineering, and assessment of safety controller engineering access, key switches and network integration. Draws on the Triton/TRISIS incident as a reference case. General OT risk methodology belongs to ICSIOT-OT-RISK.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to safety instrumented system security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands what a SIS does and why its compromise threatens life and the environment
evidence: Can explain the role of a SIS, safety instrumented functions and safety integrity levels (SIL)
Can summarise the Triton/TRISIS attack and the safety controller weaknesses it exploited
Knows that IEC 61511 requires a security risk assessment of the SIS

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Contributes to SIS security reviews under supervision
evidence: Documents SIS architecture: integrated vs. interfaced vs. air-gapped designs and their conduits to the BPCS
Reviews safety controller key switch, engineering workstation and program-mode procedures with guidance
Identifies where a SIS shares network, engineering or HMI infrastructure with the process control system
Records findings in terms that both safety and security engineers can act on

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses SIS security and safety-security interactions
evidence: Performs the IEC 61511 SIS security risk assessment, linking threat scenarios to hazards in the HAZOP/LOPA
Evaluates segregation, engineering access control and change detection for safety controllers
Assesses whether security countermeasures could degrade safety functions (and vice versa)
Produces SIS security assessment reports with recommendations agreed with functional safety engineers

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Leads SIS security assessments and co-engineering; mentors others
evidence: Leads safety-security co-engineering workshops across the lifecycle (design, FAT/SAT, operation, modification)
Assesses SIS security in a lab safety controller environment, including logic integrity verification and mode-change monitoring
Translates incidents such as Triton/TRISIS into concrete test cases and detection requirements
Mentors staff on working safely with safety controllers and with functional safety teams

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's SIS security practice; recognised authority
evidence: Established the lab's SIS security assessment and safety-security co-engineering methodology
Published research or contributed to standards on SIS security or safety-security alignment
Recognised authority consulted on SIS architecture and incident lessons
Trains teams on SIS security and safety-security integration

assessment_methods.description: Given a plant architecture with an integrated SIS and its HAZOP extract, perform a SIS security risk assessment and identify the conduits and engineering paths that could defeat a safety instrumented function
Review a SIS security assessment for coverage of IEC 61511 security requirements, linkage of threats to hazards, and recommendations that do not compromise functional safety
